# v2.92-dev

Security hardening release, continuing the review that produced v2.88-dev
through v2.91-dev. This one covers how the server's own scheduled jobs prove who
they are, and what the bulk-import endpoints will accept. It also fixes a
scheduled job that had never actually been running.

Following this project's convention for security fixes, the notes below say what
changed and what it means for you, without the technical detail of what was
wrong. **Updating promptly is recommended.**

## Fixed

- **The daily credential health check now actually runs.** The scheduled job that
  keeps the Box / OneDrive / Google Drive / SMTP status badges and the expiry
  banner up to date was being turned away before it reached the application, so
  those statuses only ever refreshed when someone pressed **Test Connection** or
  a scheduled export happened to run. It works from this release; nothing needs
  configuring. If you have cloud credentials connected, expect the health panel
  to become accurate within a day of updating.

## Hardened

- **Scheduled jobs now prove themselves per request.** The internal
  authentication used by the automatic backup, export and credential-check jobs
  previously produced one value that was good for every one of those jobs for a
  whole day. It is now tied to the individual request and to a short time
  window, and is accepted only once — so it cannot be observed and reused. This
  is entirely internal; there is nothing to configure and `CRON_SECRET` is
  unchanged.

- **Imports reject oversized and malformed uploads properly.** Every import
  endpoint now checks the size of the data before reading it in (32 MB by
  default, adjustable with the new optional `IMPORT_MAX_BODY_MB` setting) and
  returns a clear message for a file that is too large or a request that isn't
  valid import data. Previously an oversized import was read into memory in full
  before any limit applied, and a corrupt one produced a generic server error
  instead of an explanation.

- **A company-scoped report query now fails safe.** One reporting helper would
  have ignored the company filter rather than returning nothing if it were ever
  called with an empty selection. No page reached it that way, so no data was
  exposed; the guard means a future caller can't reintroduce the possibility.

## Upgrading

No database changes; the update applies automatically.

- The scheduled-job change updates the app and its cron scripts together. If a
  job happens to fire during the few minutes between the files updating and the
  service restarting, that one run is skipped and logged — exports retry the
  next minute, and the credential check retries the next day.
- `IMPORT_MAX_BODY_MB` is optional and documented in `.env.example`; the default
  suits typical imports.

The import limit and the credential-health fix are reflected in the README and
the in-app help (**Import Data** and **Scheduled Report Exports**).
